title: Advice rules — best interests duty, SoA and replacement advice
version: Rule guide FY2026-27 v1.0 — current at 23 Nov 2026 (Corporations Act compilation in force 19 Sep to 30 Nov 2026)
summary: The rules Amelia follows when she gives personal advice on life insurance, and that the Paraplanning Agent applies when it drafts a Statement of Advice (SoA): the best interests duty and the related obligations, what an SoA must contain and when it must be given, when a Record of Advice (RoA) can be used, the extra disclosure for replacement advice, and record keeping. Agents draft and check against these rules; only Amelia gives advice and signs the SoA.
limits: AI agents never give personal advice, never sign or send an SoA, and never tell a client to replace or cancel cover. An SoA can't be combined with an FSG or a PDS. The small-investment exemption doesn't apply to life risk advice. An RoA can't be used when the client's relevant circumstances or the basis of the advice have changed significantly. Proposed tranche 2 changes must not be presented as law.
evidenceRequired: Fact find: objectives, financial situation, needs and relevant circumstances
Needs analysis with the working shown
Existing cover details, and the s947D disclosures for any replacement
Commission in dollars and the client's informed consent
SoA signed by Amelia, and the client's Authority to Proceed
